key_insight: A parameter-free ab initio transport framework shows that molecular-semiconductor charge mobility emerges from the full electron–phonon spectrum, revealing nonperturbative dynamics and a revised mechanism for DNTT.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable screening and design of high-mobility organic semiconductors for transistors and photovoltaics by linking atomic structure directly to measurable transport behavior.
method: Compute electron–phonon Hamiltonians from first principles.
Propagate carriers in hundreds-of-molecule domains with the full phonon spectrum.
Use nonperturbative Green–Kubo dynamics to extract transport regimes and bottlenecks.
evidence_signal: Across five representative crystals, the approach reproduces measured mobilities, temperature exponents, and optical-conductivity fingerprints.
watch_item: The method is computationally demanding and requires high-quality ab initio electron–phonon inputs, so scaling to very large screening campaigns may be challenging.
paper_title: First-Principles Origins of Charge Transport in Molecular Semiconductors
